title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.67). A_*^• is a cosimplicial-in-*, cochain-in-• differential algebra: A_m^• is a 'de Rham complex on the m-simplex', as in Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(m,•). C^•_{*M} is the analogous object of M-valued simplicial cochains on the standard simplices Δ_m. A 'system of Stokes–De Rham integrals' is a family k_n : A_n^n → M (integration over the n-simplex) satisfying Stokes' formula. Such a system is the same as a morphism A_*^• → C^•_{*M} of (semi)cosimplicial cochain complexes, with k_0 being the augmentation.

On this page Grothendieck checks when this morphism lands in the normalized (non-degenerate) cochains C^{n!}_{*M}, i.e. the intersection of the kernels of σ^* over all σ: Δ_n→Δ_m with m<n.
- Hom(A^n_*, C^{n!}_{*M}) consists of the f with σ^*f = 0 for such σ.
- The component A^n_m → C^n_m, evaluated on the degenerate n-simplex σ of Δ_m, is the composite A^n_m --σ^*--> A^n_n --k_n--> M.
- Hence f lands in C^{n!} iff k_n∘σ^* = 0 for all σ: Δ_n→Δ_m with m<n. It suffices to test codegeneracies, since every non-injective map factors through one.
- This holds automatically when A^n_m = 0 for m<n, i.e. there are no n-forms on a lower-dimensional simplex. That was hypothesis a).

The previous page identifies C^{n!}_{*M} ≅ Λ^{*+1}Φ_* ⊗ M. Non-degenerate n-simplices of Δ_m are (n+1)-subsets of {0..m}, so normalized cochains are exterior powers of the free module Φ_m on the vertices; this is the combinatorial shadow of Whitney forms.

Example. Let S be a ring with a PD ideal J and t ∈ J. Take the divided-power polynomial de Rham algebra on the 'simplex of size t':
- A^•_{mS} = (Γ^*(Φ_{mS}) ⊗_S Λ Ψ_{mS}) / (T − t)_pd.
- Here Φ_m is free on the vertex coordinates T_0..T_m, Ψ = dΦ, T = ΣT_i, and the quotient is by the PD-differential ideal generated by T − t.
- The PD Poincaré lemma makes it a resolution of S, and A^i_j = 0 for i>j.
- So it carries an S-valued Stokes–De Rham integration system, giving A^n_* → Λ^{*+1}_S Φ_{*S}, an integral/PD de Rham-to-normalized-cochain map.

The reason t must lie in the PD ideal is implicit but clear: the Dirichlet integral over {ΣT_i = t} of T^{[a]} dT_1…dT_n equals t^{[|a|+n]}. This exists in S exactly because t has divided powers; one cannot take t = 1. The page ends by flagging the multiplicative properties (wedge product vs. cup product) as to be studied.
errors: Transcription writes f^n(A^n_*) ⊂ C^n_*; it must be the normalized C^{n!}_*. The condition is about landing in non-degenerate cochains.

Minor: the composite should read A^n_m --σ^*--> A^n_n --k_n--> M, with σ: Δ_n → Δ_m. The direction is correct in the image; the logic is fine. Restricting to codegeneracies is justified because every non-injective σ factors through a codegeneracy.

ideas.what: Criterion for the integration map from a simplicial cochain algebra to cochains to land in normalized cochains: k_n∘σ^* = 0 for degeneracies, automatic if A^n_m=0 for m<n
ideas.modern_name: de Rham/integration map into normalized cochains (Sullivan, Bousfield–Gugenheim, Félix–Halperin–Thomas)

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a 'system of Stokes–De Rham integrals' k_n: A_n^n→M as a morphism of semi-cosimplicial cochain complexes
ideas.modern_name: integration map / simplicial de Rham theorem for extendable simplicial cochain algebras

ideas.what: Identification of normalized cochains of the standard cosimplicial simplex with exterior powers Λ^{n+1}Φ_m of the free module on vertices
ideas.modern_name: Whitney elementary forms / normalized cochains of Δ[m]

ideas.what: Divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on a 'simplex of size t' (ΣT_i = t, t in a PD ideal) as an S-integral resolution with an S-valued integration (Stokes) map
ideas.modern_name: integral / PD polynomial de Rham forms on simplices; integral Sullivan-type model of cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (related ideas: Cenkl–Porter integral/tame de Rham forms 1981; Karoubi's de Rham with arbitrary coefficients 1990s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs a de Rham-to-cochain integration map over any PD ring S. It uses divided-power polynomial forms on the deformed simplex ΣT_i = t with t ∈ J, so integrals land in S via t^{[n+|a|]}. He explicitly leaves its multiplicative properties (compatibility of wedge product with cup product, up to homotopy / E∞ structure) unstudied.
missed.quote: A^*_{*S} = (Γ^*(Φ_{*S}) ⊗_S Λ Ψ_{*S})/(T−t)_pd, c'est une résolution de S, et A^i_j = 0 si i > j ... dont il faudrait étudier les propriétés multiplicatives...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Commutative cochain models over Z or Z_p are a live topic (Mandell's E∞ p-adic homotopy theory; divided-power/Γ-algebra models; integral Sullivan models). A PD-commutative de Rham model of cochains over a PD base, with the 'simplex of size t ∈ J' trick to make integration integral, links crystalline/PD de Rham technology to integral homotopy theory. I do not know a published source with this exact construction.

missed.claim: Implicit link between the crystalline PD de Rham complex (Berthelot/Grothendieck) and Sullivan–Whitney simplicial de Rham theory. The PD condition t ∈ J is exactly what makes the Dirichlet simplex integral integral.
missed.quote: Soit S un anneau à p.d. J, t ∈ J ... système d'intégrales de Stokes-De Rham à valeurs dans S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a concrete mechanism for comparing PD/crystalline-type de Rham complexes with singular cochains integrally. It is relevant to current interest in integral and p-adic comparison maps.

deep.surprise_reason: The verification itself is routine. The example is notable: divided-power polynomial forms on a simplex of 'size t' with t in a PD ideal, giving an integral Stokes/de Rham integration map over an arbitrary PD ring. This is a neat and, to my knowledge, unpublished 1976 anticipation of integral commutative cochain models. It is only sketched, and its multiplicative behaviour is left open.
transcription_corrections: 'qui sont autres [?] que le composé' is likely 'qui sont autres que [i.e. ne sont autres que] le composé', meaning 'which are none other than the composite'.
'Soit S un anneau à p.d. [?] J, v.i. [?]' is probably 'un anneau à p.d. (J, γ)' or similar.
'l'anneau différentiel k [?] à p.d.' is probably 'anneau différentiel gradué (simplicial) à p.d.'.
The arrow at the bottom goes from the PD de Rham algebra to Λ^{*+1}_S Φ_{*S} (normalized S-cochains), not an isomorphism to it.
